records.title: Water conservation: water wise designation.
records.description: (Informational, on the horizon) The State Water Resources Control Board, in conjunction with the Department of Water Resources, must establish long-term standards and performance measures for efficient water use, focusing on commercial, industrial, and institutional (CII) sectors by June 30, 2022. The department is also required, by October 1, 2021, to conduct research and offer recommendations for these standards. This bill mandates a statewide "water wise" designation, to be included in the Save Our Water Campaign, recognizing CII sector businesses that adhere to or surpass recommended best water management practices.
status_samples: In committee: Set, first hearing. Hearing canceled at the request of author.

records.title: Single-family and multifamily housing units: preapproved plans.
records.description: By January 1, 2025, local agencies must create programs for preapproving ADU plans. By July 1, 2026, local agencies must also develop programs for preapproving single-family and multifamily residential housing plans. Local agencies can charge fees for these preapprovals and must post approved plans and applicant contact information online. Agencies must approve or deny applications within 30 days if conditions are met. The bill allows agencies to accept additional plans at their discretion without density limits. Preapproved projects under this bill are exempt from CEQA.

records.title: Regional housing needs: regional transportation plan.
records.description: Requires HCD to determine each region's housing needs at least 3 years (instead of 2) prior to scheduled housing element revisions. Requires COGs to consult with HCD earlier  and consider the development pattern in the region's sustainable communities strategy when allocating housing needs. Requires that the housing allocation plan be "informed by" rather than strictly "consistent with" the transportation strategy, giving slightly more flexibility to local governments.

records.title: Planning and zoning: housing development: standardized application form.
records.description: mandates that by July 1, 2027, HCD will adopt a standardized application form for housing entitlements, which cities and counties must accept starting October 1, 2027, prohibiting them from requiring additional forms unless absolutely necessary. The bill clarifies that an application for a housing entitlement is considered complete upon payment of fees and submission of specified basic information, such as a project description and a list of requested approvals, with certain exceptions for specific jurisdictions. It further prohibits local governments from requiring certain information or approvals as a condition for deeming an application complete and prevents them from penalizing applicants who use the standardized form. The bill also strengthens enforcement by adding violations of these new housing application requirements to the list of offenses that can trigger notification to the Attorney General. Additionally, it revises the definition of "disapprove the housing development project" under the Housing Accountability Act to include instances where a local agency improperly deems an application incomplete

records.description: Would correct references in the Housing Accountability Act related to the "builder's remedy project" and applicant obligation to resubmit information for housing projects.

records.title: California Environmental Quality Act: notice: direct mailing: electronic mail.
records.description: Would allow CEQA EIRS, Neg Decs, or making other determinations to be sent by email if the recipient has requested this form of communication.

records.title: General plan: annual report: congregate and residential care for the elderly.
records.description: amends existing law to allow local governments, when revising their housing elements for the seventh time and subsequent revisions, to include the number of approved units for congregate care for the elderly, as defined by Section 50062.5 of the Health and Safety Code, as part of their annual report to the state. This inclusion can account for up to 15% of a jurisdiction's allocated regional housing need for any income category. Congregate care for the elderly refers to housing that provides both shelter and supportive services for older adults. This change aims to provide more flexibility in how local governments report on their progress in meeting housing needs, particularly for seniors.

records.title: Land use: housing elements: target population.
records.description: HE must analyze needs for special housing, emergency shelters, and supportive housing. The law also defines "target population" for housing needs, including low-income individuals with disabilities and those eligible for certain disability services. The proposed bill seeks to expand the term "target population" to also cover victims of domestic violence. This addition imposes extra obligations on local governments regarding housing plans, thus creating a state-mandated local program. According to the California Constitution, the state must reimburse local agencies and schools for specific state-mandated costs. The bill ensures that if state-mandated costs are identified, reimbursement will occur following existing statutory procedures.

records.title: Data centers: monthly reporting.
records.description: mandates that the State Energy Resources Conservation and Development Commission, known as the Energy Commission, creates a process for data center owners to submit monthly reports on their energy and water usage, including power usage effectiveness, water usage effectiveness, total water consumption, and fuel consumption by onsite generators. The Commission must also include an assessment of data center electrical load trends in its 2029 integrated energy policy report and publish the submitted information, anonymized and aggregated, annually online. When applying for permits, data center owners must provide specified information to local agencies, who can use it for planning and environmental assessments. The bill ensures this information is not disclosed in a manner revealing personal or specific utility data. Legislative findings justify restricting access to certain public meetings and records. The bill states no reimbursement is required by this act, according to the California Constitution, which mandates reimbursement for certain state-imposed costs on local agencies and school districts.

records.title: Planning and Zoning Law: postentitlement phase permits: Housing Accountability Act.
records.description: Would  prohibit a local agency from requiring/requesting more than 2 plan checks and specification reviews for an application for a building permit. Would authorize a local agency to deny an application that is not compliant with the permit standards following more than 2 plan checks and specification reviews.

records.title: Public Lands Protection Act.
records.description: This bill, known as the Public Lands Protection Act, proposes if a parcel of federal land has already been designated as open space, public land, resource conservation, or a similar conservation category, it will be subject to those existing restrictions upon transfer to private or nonfederal ownership. If the land has not been zoned, it will automatically receive the most restrictive conservation zoning designation within local jurisdiction.

records.title: Western Joshua Tree Conservation Act: removal: trimming.
records.description: Amends the WJT Conservation Act to create new exemptions and permit conditions for the removal or trimming of WJT. Specifically, exempts projects or activities on parcels with a SFR that has been continuously owned by the same person since before July 10, 2023, provided local ordinances regarding these trees are followed on that date. Additionally, CDFW can now issue permits, without fees or mitigation, for the removal or trimming of WJT if they are on a parcel with an occupied SFR that qualifies for a homeowner's property tax exemption, and the work is necessary for maintaining, repairing, or replacing existing infrastructure or utilities, or for fire safety requirements, with a limit of 10 trees per permit. The bill also clarifies permit application requirements, including photographic evidence and attestations, and streamlines the process for certain types of tree removal requests.

records.title: Accelerated retailer building plan approval: tenant improvements.
records.description: Would establish an accelerated approval process for building permits for "tenant improvements"(changes to the interior of an existing building), specifically for "retailers," (any business selling directly to the public). Modeled after a restaurants process. This bill allows a "qualified professional certifier" to review/certify that the plans for a retailer's tenant improvement comply with all applicable building codes at the applicant's expense. The local building department must then approve or deny the permit within 20 business days; if they fail to do so, the plan is considered approved. If denied, resubmissions are limited to addressing the initial deficiencies and must be reviewed within 10 business days.

records.title: Housing developments: ordinances, policies, and standards.
records.description: The HAA requires a housing project to be subject only to the ordinances, policies, and standards adopted and in effect when a prelim app is submitted. Bill would amend definition to include "materials, requirements and postentitlement permit standards" within "ordinances, policies, and standards" that housing projects must adhere to.

records.title: California Environmental Quality Act: exemption: housing development project: public higher education land use plan.
records.description: Would make housing projects consistent with public higher education land use plans or those meeting specific state standards for infill projects CEQA exempt.

records.title: State Housing Law: remote inspections.
records.description: This bill would require a county to offer homeowners the option of requesting remote insepctions for all or a subset of an inspection required by a building permit for specified works in one or 2 family dwelling units by July 1,2027. Local agencies must report annually to the HCD on their implmentation of remote inspections, and HCD must publicize these reports online. The bill grants HCD authority to gather info to ensure complaince and undertake enforcementas needed.

records.title: Missing Middle Townhome Ownership Act.
records.description: This bill, the Missing Middle Townhome Ownership Act allows for a streamlined approval process for townhome projects that meet specific criteria, including density requirements and parcel sizes. The bill permits local agencies to adopt implementing ordinances, which are not subject to CEQA review.

records.title: Public agencies: approval: detention facilities.
records.description: Would require counties to follow a more extensive 180-day public notification and comment process before approving any documents related to the building or reuse of existing facilities by private entities for housing or detaining individuals

records.title: Land use: mitigation lands.
records.description: Would remove the expiration date  that allow various entities, including government agencies to hold and manage funds (endowments) set aside for the long-term care of "mitigation lands" (properties set aside to offset environmental impacts from development projects.) Removing the January 1, 2027 repeal date, extends mechanisms for managing conservation funds indefinitely.

records.title: Western Joshua Tree Conservation Act: industrial projects and commercial projects: single-family residences: public works projects.
records.description:
Expands existing WJT authority by allowing cities to authorize the removal of WJT for commercial and industrial projects, in addition to the SFR, multi-family residences, accessory structures, and public works projects already covered. Also introduces new provisions that allows, without requiring fees or further mitigation:
- homeowners of existing SFRs to remove or trim WJT within 30 ft of their home or 15 ft of an existing or proposed accessory structure
- allows developers of public works projects to remove or trim trees within their construction footprint or 15 ft of it
.... provided they submit specific information to CDFW and receive a permit within 60 days.

records.title: Factory-built housing: building standards.
records.description: Would streamline the construction of factory-built housing by preventing local governments from imposing stricter building standards than those set by the state.

records.title: Electric vehicle charging stations: permit fees.
records.description: Limits permit fees local govts can charge for EV charging stations. Until January 1, 2036, counties cannot charge more than the reasonable cost of providing the permitting service, with specific caps based on kW. Local govts can exceed these limits if they provide adopted resolution/ordinance with substantial evidence.

records.title: California Public Records Act: agency response time.
records.description: Under the California Public Records Act, agencies must provide promptly copies of reasonably described public records on request and, within 10 calendar days, must determine whether requested records are disclosable and notify the requester; that 10‑day period may be extended by up to 14 calendar days for unusual circumstances. The bill changes those timing rules to require the initial determination and notice within 10 business days and allows extensions of up to 14 business days

records.title: Subdivisions: tentative and final map: exceptions.
records.description: The Subdivision Map Act mandates that tentative and final maps be prepared for certain subdivisions, like those with five or more parcels or condominiums, unless specific exceptions apply. One such exception includes land zoned for industrial or commercial purposes with approved access to public streets and governing body approval on street dimensions. In these cases, only a parcel map is required. The bill proposes expanding this exception to also include land zoned for mixed-use development, as long as the other existing conditions are still met.

records.title: California Environmental Quality Act: exemption: passenger rail service.
records.description: Removes the requirement that an entire passenger rail service  project must be exclusively used by zero-emission trains or cleaner locomotives, and instead only requires the mainline rail to be located within an existing right-of-way or highway right-of-way. Additionally, it allows projects that would otherwise be ineligible due to their use of non-zero-emission trains in air basins with poor air quality to be exempt if they establish new daily passenger rail service between distant points and run parallel to a highway corridor.

records.title: Wildfire prevention: local assistance grant program: eligible activities.
records.description: Expand eligible activities for Dept Forestry and Fire Protection grants to include projects by local government entities for acquiring or installing mobile or permanent infrastructure, like mobile rigid dip tanks, that can provide helicopter-accessible water supplies for firefighting in high fire hazard areas.

records.title: Surplus Land Act: exemptions: land unsuitable for housing.
records.description: This bill amends the Surplus Land Act, which governs how local government agencies sell or lease surplus land, by adding a new category of "exempt surplus land." This exemption applies to land that is unsuitable for housing development due to specific characteristics, such as slope instability that poses seismic risks, inclusion in a Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) flood hazard zone, location in a high or very high fire hazard severity zone, or the presence of sensitive ecological habitats like wetlands.

records.title: General plan elements: childcare.
records.description: mandates that when a county updates two or more elements in their general plan after January 1, 2028, they must also update those elements to address childcare needs, ensuring access to quality, convenient, safe, and affordable childcare

records.title: Short-term rentals: emergencies and special events.
records.description: OES will manage a system for emergency situations, allowing registered "eligible residential dwellings" to be offered as short-term rentals immediately upon registration, overriding local prohibitions.

records.title: Streets and highways: pedestrian and bicycle facilities.
records.description: Would prohibit local govts from holding public input meetings on pedestrian or bicycle safety projects after they've been included in an approved general plan. Revises the "Pedestrian Mall Law of 1960" into the "Pedestrian Mall Law of 2026," streamlining the process for establishing pedestrian malls by removing certain notice and hearing requirements, while allowing private businesses to use and improve these spaces.

records.title: Land use: housing development approvals: timelines and processes.
records.description:
1. Prohibits one local utility or agency from overturning approvals made by another unless the project proponent makes a significant change. 
2. Would award extra points for state housing programs to jurisdictions that are designated as "housing development expediters" by HCD. 
3. For counties with populations of 250,000+, the bill mandates the assignment of a project development director to oversee projects costing over $10 million from application to occupancy, and a lead inspector to coordinate inspections. 
4. Would shorten the timeframes for local agencies to approve or disapprove development projects after environmental reviews are completed.

records.title: local gov't assistance: Regional Early Action Planning Fund.
records.description: Establishes the Regional Early Action Planning  (REAP) Fund to provide one-time funding and grants for planning activities related to the 7th and future cycles of the regional need assessment.
